objects.description: Stateless functor implementing MurmurHash2 hashing. Provides overloaded operator() for strings, C-style strings, raw byte arrays, integral types, pointers, thread IDs, and smart pointers. Optimized for short inputs via inlining and loop unrolling. No constructors or state; safe to copy and use as a hasher in associative containers. Destruction has no special requirements. Template helper is_char_v is an internal detail.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: size_t nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(const std::string& str) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes a std::string using a MurmurHash2-based implementation. Optimized for short strings and inlinable. Intended as a fast general-purpose hash for string keys.
requirements: str.data() must point to at least str.length() readable bytes.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.
May be called from multiple threads; the functor is stateless.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename = std::enable_if_t<is_char_v<T>>> size_t nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(const T*& str) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes a null-terminated C-style string (pointer passed by reference) of character type using MurmurHash2. The pointer itself is not modified; the reference allows overload resolution to prefer null-terminated strings.
requirements: T must be one of char, signed char, or unsigned char.
str must be non-null and point to a null-terminated byte string; memory must be readable up to and including the terminating '\0'.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename = std::enable_if_t<is_char_v<T>>> size_t nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(const T* str, size_t size) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes a raw byte buffer of character type with explicit size using a MurmurHash2 64-bit style mix (fixed seed). Suitable for hashing arbitrary bytes.
requirements: T must be one of char, signed char, or unsigned char.
str may be null only if size == 0; otherwise str must point to at least size readable bytes.
The function reads the buffer as 64-bit chunks internally; the provided memory must be valid and accessible for the given size.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.description: Hashes a std::thread::id by delegating to std::hash<std::thread::id>(). Useful for using thread IDs as keys in hash-based containers.
requirements: No preconditions on id; any valid std::thread::id is accepted.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: template <size_t N, typename T, typename = std::enable_if_t<is_char_v<T>>> size_t nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(const T (&str)[N]) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes a character array (e.g., string literal) without decay, treating it as a null-terminated string of length N-1. This avoids a runtime strlen for literals.
requirements: T must be one of char, signed char, or unsigned char.
str must reference an array of size N whose last element is the null terminator when used as a C string; the function hashes the first N-1 elements.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: template <typename T> std::enable_if_t<std::is_integral<T>::value, size_t> nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(T key) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes an integral value by casting it to size_t. Intended for quickly hashing integer keys without additional mixing.
requirements: T must be an integral type (std::is_integral<T>::value == true).
Be aware that negative values (for signed T) will be converted to size_t by implementation-defined unsigned conversion.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: template <typename T> std::enable_if_t<!is_char_v<T>, size_t> nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(const T* ptr) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes a non-character typed pointer by reinterpreting the address as size_t. The pointed-to data is not read.
requirements: T must not be a character type (char, signed char, unsigned char).
ptr may be null; only the pointer value is used.
No alignment or lifetime requirements beyond having a representable pointer value; the object is not dereferenced.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

functions.name: nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()
functions.signature: template <typename T> size_t nebula::MurmurHash2::operator()(const std::shared_ptr<T>& ptr) const noexcept
functions.description: Hashes a std::shared_ptr by hashing its underlying raw pointer address (ptr.get()). The managed object is not inspected.
requirements: ptr may be empty (null); only ptr.get() is used.
Hash equality follows pointer identity, not object value semantics.
Function is noexcept and does not throw.

data_types.description: A buffer of raw bytes with an explicit length. May contain any values including NUL bytes and is not required to be valid text or encoded content. Suitable for APIs that take (ptr, size) and treat input as opaque bytes.

A C-style string terminated by a NUL byte. Memory must be readable up to and including the terminating NUL; contents may be any byte sequence that includes a terminating NUL, typically used via const char* or similar.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs used by the MurmurHash2 fuzzer stub.
# The stub consumes FUZZ_PARAM_STR for s1 and s2, plus integral parameters
# via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), FUZZ_PARAM(long long), FUZZ_PARAM(int).
# Our buffer will be interpreted by the harness to sequentially satisfy
# these FUZZ_PARAM calls. We therefore craft a byte stream that contains:
# - Two interesting strings (for s1 and s2), each length-prefixed to help the
#   harness split them if it uses typical length-prefix semantics, or separated
#   with NUL so c_str() and data() are coherent and varied.
# - A few integers to feed FUZZ_PARAM integral requests. We provide enough bytes
#   so repeated integer pulls succeed. Endianness-agnostic harnesses typically
#   read little-endian; we emit little-endian.
#
# Design goals:
# - Strings cover diverse lengths and character classes, including NUL inside,
#   ASCII, extended bytes, and edge sizes (0, small, near 1024 cap).
# - Raw buffer case sometimes uses null buffer via use_null_buf decision; we
#   bias integers so that occasionally (mod 4 == 0) happens.
# - Keep total under 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_SETS = [
    string.ascii_lowercase,
    string.ascii_uppercase,
    string.digits,
    string.punctuation,
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_interesting_string(rng: random.Random, target_max: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a pattern
    patterns = [
        "empty",
        "ascii_word",
        "mixed_ascii",
        "with_nuls",
        "repeated_block",
        "utf8_like",
        "binary",
        "edge_1024",
    ]
    p = rng.choice(patterns)

    if p == "empty":
        payload = b""
    elif p == "ascii_word":
        # simple lowercase
        n = rng.randint(1, min(64, target_max))
        payload = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(n)).encode()
    elif p == "mixed_ascii":
        # mix of classes
        pool = ''.join(ASCII_SETS)
        n = rng.randint(1, min(256, target_max))
        payload = ''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n)).encode()
    elif p == "with_nuls":
        # include embedded NULs
        n = rng.randint(1, min(128, target_max))
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        remaining = n
        while remaining > 0:
            chunk = rng.randint(0, min(16, remaining))
            parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, chunk))
            remaining -= chunk
            if remaining > 0:
                # insert a NUL
                parts.append(b"\x00")
                remaining -= 1
        payload = b"".join(parts)
    elif p == "repeated_block":
        # exercise loop-unrolling by hitting multiples of 8
        block = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.choice([1, 2, 4, 8, 16]))
        reps = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(128, target_max // max(1, len(block)))))
        payload = (block * reps)[:target_max]
    elif p == "utf8_like":
        # generate valid-looking UTF-8 sequences of various lengths
        chunks: List[bytes] = []
        total = rng.randint(1, min(512, target_max))
        while len(chunks) < total:
            t = rng.random()
            if t < 0.5:
                chunks.append(bytes([rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E)]))
            elif t < 0.7:
                # 2-byte
                b1 = rng.randint(0xC2, 0xDF)
                b2 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
                chunks.append(bytes([b1, b2]))
            elif t < 0.9:
                # 3-byte
                b1 = rng.randint(0xE0, 0xEF)
                b2 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
                b3 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
                chunks.append(bytes([b1, b2, b3]))
            else:
                # 4-byte
                b1 = rng.randint(0xF0, 0xF4)
                b2 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
                b3 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
                b4 = rng.randint(0x80, 0xBF)
                chunks.append(bytes([b1, b2, b3, b4]))
            if sum(len(c) for c in chunks) > target_max:
                break
        payload = b"".join(chunks)[:target_max]
    elif p == "binary":
        n = rng.randint(1, min(512, target_max))
        payload = _rand_bytes(rng, n)
    else:  # edge_1024
        # make size near boundary 1024 where stub truncates
        n = rng.choice([1024, 1023, 1025, 1000])
        n = min(n, target_max)
        payload = _rand_bytes(rng, n)

    # Ensure within limit
    if len(payload) > target_max:
        payload = payload[:target_max]

    return payload


def _le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return int(x & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False)


def _le64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return int(x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(8, 'little', signed=False)


def _encode_len_prefixed(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return len(b).to_bytes(4, 'little') + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build s1 and s2 with diversity; fuzzer stub caps at 1024 so we target <= 1100
    s1 = _make_interesting_string(rng, 1100)
    s2 = _make_interesting_string(rng, 1100)

    # Provide integers for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), FUZZ_PARAM(long long), FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int),
    # FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), FUZZ_PARAM(int) in the stub order. We'll pack a pool of several.
    # Bias some values to trigger use_null_buf (mod 4 == 0) occasionally and other branches.
    uints: List[int] = []
    # First unsigned int: used for deciding use_null_buf
    # Make it divisible by 4 with decent probability.
    base = rng.getrandbits(32)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = (base & ~0x3)
    uints.append(base)
    # Additional unsigned ints used later (determinism asserts unaffected)
    for _ in range(4):
        v = rng.getrandbits(32)
        uints.append(v)

    # Signed long long
    sll = rng.getrandbits(64)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # make negative by setting high bit if environment treats as signed when read
        sll |= (1 << 63)

    # Signed int
    sint = rng.getrandbits(32)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sint |= (1 << 31)

    # Assemble buffer. We choose a simple layout understood by many fuzz harnesses:
    # [len32][s1][NUL][len32][s2][NUL][uint32 * N][int64][uint32 * M][int32]
    # Even if the harness does not use length prefixes, the presence of NUL ensures
    # c_str() works and truncation points are available.

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # s1 with explicit length and a trailing NUL to ensure C-string path is valid
    parts.append(_encode_len_prefixed(s1))
    parts.append(b"\x00")

    # s2 similarly
    parts.append(_encode_len_prefixed(s2))
    parts.append(b"\x00")

    # Pack several unsigned ints
    for v in uints:
        parts.append(_le32(v))

    # Pack signed long long as 64-bit two's complement (consumer may read as bytes)
    parts.append(_le64(sll))

    # Another unsigned int (already provided a pool; include a couple extra)
    parts.append(_le32(rng.getrandbits(32)))
    parts.append(_le32(rng.getrandbits(32)))

    # Signed int
    parts.append(_le32(sint))

    buf = b"".join(parts)

    # Cap to MAX_TOTAL
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return buf
